sentences.text: For centuries in Europe, most books were copied by hand, letter by letter.
A single book could take months, so books were rare and often expensive.
Around the year 1440, Johannes Gutenberg, a craftsman in Germany, built a press that changed the pace.
He did not invent the whole idea of printing. People in East Asia had already printed with carved blocks.
Gutenberg's important idea was movable metal type: separate metal letters that could be arranged into words.
A worker could set a page, ink it, press paper against it, and later set a different page with the same letters.
The ink was thick and oily so it would cling to the metal and print a clean mark.
Because the letters could be used again, a workshop could produce many copies of the same book.
Copies still had to be checked. A mistake in the type would show up on every printed page.
Even so, books became faster to make and, over time, easier for more people to own.
More books helped more people practice reading, and ideas could travel farther than one handwritten copy.
The press did not make everyone agree. It made it easier for many different voices to be written down.
Newspapers, schoolbooks, and short pamphlets later grew from this faster way of putting words on paper.
Printing can be digital now, but a great change began when letters became pieces a person could move.

questions.prompt: What is this passage mostly about?

choices.text: How movable type made books faster to produce
How carved blocks were first used on the moon
Why ink should be as thin as water
How handwriting became slower after 1440

questions.explanation: The passage contrasts slow hand copying with Gutenberg's reusable metal letters and the books that followed. Faster production is the main idea.

questions.prompt: About what year did Gutenberg build his press?

choices.text: Around 1040
Around 1440
Around 1840
Around 1940

questions.explanation: The passage places the press around the year 1440 in Germany. The other dates are not the one given.

questions.prompt: Movable type in this passage means what?

choices.text: A book copied slowly by one hand
Ink that never dries on paper
Separate letters that can be arranged and reused
A carved block that cannot be changed

questions.explanation: The passage defines movable metal type as separate metal letters that can be arranged into words and used again for another page.

questions.prompt: Why would one mistake in the metal type matter so much?

choices.text: The mistake would appear on only one handwritten page
Readers would be unable to see any ink
The press would turn the mistake into a picture
Every copy of that page would show the same mistake

questions.explanation: The passage says a mistake in the type would show up on every printed page. A reader can figure out that reusable type spreads a single error to the whole batch.

questions.prompt: Which of these came first in the passage?

choices.text: Books in Europe were copied by hand
Gutenberg built his press
Newspapers grew from the faster process
The same metal letters were reused for many copies

questions.explanation: The passage begins with centuries of hand copying. Gutenberg's press, reused letters, and later newspapers all come after that beginning.
